title: A first collaboration conversation with STXBP1 Foundation

sentences.text: We invite STXBP1 Foundation to explore a practical partnership for VAMP2 families.
VAMP2 and STXBP1 help assemble SNARE machinery involved in communication between nerve cells.
The atlas also infers similar symptoms, but that connection has confidence 0.46, below 0.5, and should not be treated as proof that families have identical needs.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: VAMP2 resources include Simons Searchlight, the MRC-funded UCL–Yale VAMP2 / SNAREopathy project, and survey and natural-history studies of epilepsy-dyskinesia syndromes.
Citizen Health and RARE-X include STXBP1 families; we could explore sharing experience with these platforms rather than starting from scratch.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please confirm whether Citizen Health, RARE-X and the ENDD Center accept related conditions, including VAMP2.

Please check whether prolonged convulsive seizures (convulsive status epilepticus), repetitive hand wringing and self-injurious behavior occur in STXBP1, and clarify the seven additional symptom gaps flagged for resource reuse.
Please review differences involving an altered protein blocking the working protein and preparation of nerve-cell signal packets for release, rather than assuming identical biology.
Gain-of-function connections are contested, and the VAMP2 claim that one working copy is insufficient is atlas-inferred, unverified and below 0.5 confidence.
Before proceeding, check trial enrollment and whether a documented VAMP2 animal or cell model is accessible.
Send one inquiry to STXBP1 Foundation asking whether STARR (STXBP1 Clinical Trial Ready) could include VAMP2-related disorders.
Is any interventional trial enrolling people with VAMP2-related disorders?
Is there a documented, accessible VAMP2 animal or cell model in the atlas?
Which individual variants increase activity, impair activity or cause loss of function?
Which GBA1, HEXA, NPC1 and GAA variants might respond to protein-folding support, and should this broader question inform our collaboration?
Dear STXBP1 Foundation team,
Could we explore whether STARR could include VAMP2-related disorders?
Our genes share a role in SNARE complex assembly.
We would welcome guidance on eligibility and differences that need checking.
Could you advise on this first step this month?
[Your name], on behalf of VAMP2.org / Raging Raymond Foundation
